sources.agency: Utah Geospatial Resource Center and Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office
sources.title: Utah Vista Ballot Areas (the State Geographic Information Database)
sources.about: The voting precincts of all 29 counties as the county clerks submit them to Vista, the state's voter system; where a county splits a precinct into subprecincts, the subprecincts.

sources.agency: Utah Geospatial Resource Center and Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office
sources.title: Utah District Combination Areas 2026 (updated after the 2025 court decision)
sources.about: Every piece of the state with one combination of congressional, Utah Senate, Utah House and State Board of Education district: read as a check that each ballot area's four districts are a combination the state has.

sources.agency: Utah Geospatial Resource Center and Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office
sources.title: Utah US Congress Districts 2026 to 2032
sources.about: The four districts the Third District Court adopted in November 2025 after it set aside the Legislature's plan, used for elections from January 1, 2026.

sources.agency: Utah Geospatial Resource Center and Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office
sources.title: Utah House Districts 2022 to 2032 and Utah Senate Districts 2022 to 2032
sources.about: The 75 House and 29 Senate districts the Legislature drew after the 2020 census.

sources.agency: Utah Geospatial Resource Center and Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office
sources.title: Utah School Board Districts 2022 to 2032
sources.about: The 15 State Board of Education districts, laid over the ballot areas (the member column is never asked for).

sources.title: Utah Municipal Boundaries
sources.about: City and town limits, kept current with the boundary changes the Lieutenant Governor certifies; each keyed by the Census Bureau's place code it carries.

sources.title: Utah County Boundaries
sources.about: Read only for the area check: each county's ballot areas against the county.

sources.title: Utah Judicial Districts
sources.about: Read only for which counties make up each of the eight judicial districts, checked against Utah Code 78A-1-102; the lines drawn are the county lines.

sources.title: TIGER/Line Shapefiles 2025, unified school districts, Utah (tl_2025_49_unsd.zip)
sources.about: School district lines as the Bureau had them for the 2024-2025 school year, from the State's own reporting.

sources.title: TIGER/Line Shapefiles 2025, places, Utah (tl_2025_49_place.zip)
sources.about: Read only for whether a municipality is a city or a town, and for its name, by the place code UGRC's layer carries.

notes.lines: Every precinct line is the state layer's, generalised by at most 1.5 metres and set on a grid of 0.00001 degree (about a metre). A point within a few metres of a line can fall on either side of it.
notes.precincts: A shape is a ballot area: a precinct, or where a county clerk has split a precinct into formal subprecincts, a subprecinct (subprecincts exist so that everyone in one gets the same ballot). The county clerk is the authority on which precinct an address is in.
notes.districts: Which congressional, Utah Senate, Utah House and State Board of Education district a ballot area lies in is worked out here by laying the state's district lines over it (analysis, not an official list): the district holding most of its area. The few ballot areas with 3% or more of their area in a second district are listed under check. The congressional districts are the four the Third District Court adopted in November 2025, used from the 2026 elections.
notes.places: Utah's cities and towns, by the state's municipal boundaries. A ballot area's mcd is the place holding half or more of it (absent in unincorporated country); mcd_all lists every place it reaches where it reaches more than one or lies partly outside: to say which place a point is in, ask the mcd layer, not the precinct. A place the Census Bureau's 2025 list does not yet carry as a city or town (newly incorporated) is called a municipality; muni_vs_census under counts names the places on one list and not the other.
notes.commissioners: No statewide file has the lines of county commission or council districts; each county keeps its own.
notes.boards: The State Board of Education's 15 members are each elected by a district; sboe names the district a ballot area votes in.
notes.school: School district lines are the Census Bureau's 2025 file. Which districts a ballot area lies in is analysis, not an official list: a district counts when its part of the area is at least 60 metres thick somewhere; school_pct is each district's share of the area (land and water, not voters).
notes.judicial: The eight judicial districts are whole counties (Utah Code 78A-1-102); district and juvenile court judges stand for retention in them. A justice court judge stands for retention in the county or city the court serves.
notes.wards: No statewide file has the lines of city council districts: a council district's race is placed on its city, and the city recorder says which district an address is in.
notes.authority: For which precinct an address is in, the county clerk is the authority; for where to vote, the state's voter search and the county clerk.
notes.precinct_ids: A ballot area's id is its county's five digits, a full stop and the VistaID the state's layer gives it (49035.SLC009; 49011.6BO10:I-S- for a subprecinct).

format.files: Every file is TopoJSON on one grid (transform above): arcs are delta-encoded lines; a shape's arcs name the lines of its rings, a negative number n meaning line ~n backwards; outer rings run counter-clockwise, holes clockwise.
format.county_files: precincts/<county>.json, object 'precincts': one shape per ballot area. arcMask[i] has bit k set when line i is an outline of arc_kinds[k]; arcSides[2i] and arcSides[2i+1] are the areas on the right and left of line i (-1: an area in another county's file, or one just across a hairline gap in the state's drawing; -2: outside Utah); names gives the names of the places the file's areas lie in.
format.boxes: boxes[county] holds four whole numbers a ballot area, in the file's order: west, south, east, north in steps of box_step degrees from the transform's translate, rounded outwards. A point is tried against every area whose box (widened by half a step) holds it.

precinct_properties.name: the precinct's name: the county's own name for it where the state's layer gives one, else 'Precinct' and its code (and subprecinct)
precinct_properties.precinct: the precinct's code as the county gives it, with the subprecinct
precinct_properties.mcd: the city or town holding half or more of the area (absent in unincorporated country)
precinct_properties.mcd_all: list, where the area reaches more than one place or lies partly outside: every place it lies in, largest share first
precinct_properties.mcd_pct: list, with mcd_all: each place's share of the area, in percent
precinct_properties.sboe: State Board of Education district (UT-SBOE1 1, UT-SBOE2 2, UT-SBOE3 3, UT-SBOE4 4, UT-SBOE5 5, UT-SBOE6 6, UT-SBOE7 7, UT-SBOE8 8, UT-SBOE9 9, UT-SBOE10 10, UT-SBOE11 11, UT-SBOE12 12, UT-SBOE13 13, UT-SBOE14 14, UT-SBOE15 15)
precinct_properties.split: only where a second district holds 3 percent or more of the area: for house, senate, cd or sboe, each district's share in percent
precinct_properties.school: list: the school districts the area lies in, largest share first
precinct_properties.school_pct: list, when the area is in more than one: each district's share of its area, in percent
precinct_properties.school_out: percent of the area that lies in no school district (given from 3 percent up)
precinct_properties.school_edge: list: neighbouring districts that only brush the area along a line (try them too when placing a point)
precinct_properties.c: a point inside the area's largest part, for a label: [longitude, latitude]

ids.every layer: a shape's properties j and d are the jurisdiction id and the district its races carry on the ballot pages
ids.mcd: UT-M- and the Census Bureau's place code (UT-M-67000), or UGRC's code for a place the Bureau has no code for yet; properties.t says city or town (municipality: incorporated after the Bureau's 2025 list)
ids.cd: the district (1); properties.race is the race for Congress
ids.judicial: JD and the district's number (JD3); d is the number
ids.school: UT-S- and the Census Bureau's five-digit district code; properties.nces is the federal district code
ids.sboe: a precinct property only: UT-SBOE and the district's number (UT-SBOE7)
